contradictions.fact: total gain for the full trip

claims.says: roughly 27 miles round trip with ~7,300 ft of gain for the full trip
roughly 21-27 miles, 7,000-8,000+ ft of gain

contradictions.why: The route's own approach text and pro_tips both cite ~7,000-8,000+ ft of total gain, which matches the loss_ft value (7300) almost exactly rather than the stated gain_ft (6013), a ~20% discrepancy for a round-trip that should have gain roughly equal to loss.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Approach text and pro_tips (~7,300 ft) agree with loss_ft (7300); gain_ft (6013) is the outlier and looks mislabeled or stale.

claims.says: ~10.3 mi one-way on maintained Wolf Creek Trail #527...to Gardner Meadows
roughly 27 miles round trip with ~7,300 ft of gain for the full trip
roughly 21-27 miles, 7,000-8,000+ ft of gain
12.03 (one-way, summit, 'from track')

contradictions.why: The header Dist stat (from dist_km) would show ~10.3 miles, but that number matches only the one-way trail distance to Gardner Meadows (not the summit); the route's own prose and the summit waypoint's one-way distance (12.03 mi, ~24 mi round trip) both indicate the true round trip is roughly 21-27 miles — off by more than 2x.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The summit waypoint's one-way distance (12.03 mi) doubled (~24 mi) agrees with the approach/pro_tips prose (21-27 mi); dist_km (10.3 mi) matches only the trail-to-camp segment and is the outlier.

claims.says: hike all ~24 miles round trip out on day 2
Capable of 20-24+ mile round trip days

contradictions.why: The header Dist stat (from dist_km) would show ~6.2 miles total, nearly 4x shorter than the ~24-mile round trip the route's own itinerary day breakdown, totalNote, and partner requirements all agree on.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Itinerary day miles (9.5+14.5=24), totalNote, and partner_requirements all agree at ~20-24 mi; dist_km is the clear outlier.

claims.says: ~5,800 ft total gain

contradictions.why: The itinerary's own day-by-day gain/loss sums to ~5,800 ft (matching the trailhead-to-summit elevation difference of ~3,000→8,800 ft), an ~16% disagreement with the header gain_ft/loss_ft fields (4987).
contradictions.internal_resolution: Itinerary day sums and totalNote (~5,800 ft), consistent with simple trailhead-to-summit elevation arithmetic, agree with each other; gain_ft/loss_ft (4987) is the outlier.

a mile and a half of valley trail reaches the Oval Creek fork

contradictions.fact: whether a wilderness permit is required

claims.says: No wilderness permit is required in the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness. Some trailheads require a pass to park.
Free, self-issued wilderness permit at the trailhead register; no quota or advance reservation required

contradictions.fact: trailhead and pass used by the standard route

claims.says: Cottonwood Camp Trailhead
From the Entiat River/Cottonwood Camp Trailhead
Northwest Forest Pass required; ~38 mi up FS Road 51 from the town of Entiat to reach the TH.
From the Entiat River Trailhead, follow the Entiat River Trail then climb toward Emerald Park and the Saska/Borealis Ridge area...
Steep, loose scree ascending/traversing north from the saddle below Borealis Pass toward the base of Pinnacle's summit ridge.
Class 2-3 off-trail ridge/talus scramble from Borealis Pass; no rope typically carried.
North Fork Entiat Trailhead (end of FR 5606, elev 3940)
North Fork Entiat over Saska Pass and Snow Brushy Creek
Saska Pass

contradictions.why: A climber following the itinerary/timing/approach_logistics would drive to the Entiat River Trailhead and hike via Emerald Park to 'Borealis Pass', but the route's own GPS waypoints, approach_variants, and bail/descent_text are all written for a different trailhead and pass (North Fork Entiat Trailhead via Saska Pass and the Snow Brushy Creek burn crossing) — a party could drive to the wrong trailhead entirely.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The 6 GPS-located waypoints, approach_variants baseFinding, and bivy notes (reached via 'Fox Camp' off the North Fork Entiat Trail) all consistently describe the North Fork Entiat/Saska Pass line, and its cumulative mileage/gain (13.8 mi, 5,722 ft) match the route's own gain_ft/dist_km; the itinerary/timing/pitch_detail/rope_note language naming the Entiat River Trailhead and 'Borealis Pass' looks like contamination from a neighboring peak (Emerald/Cardinal, which share the same Fox Camp basin per the bivy notes).

claims.says: Hike the Crater Creek/Crater Lakes Trail about 3.9 miles one-way...to Crater Lake, then continue off-trail up the southeast ridge to the ~8,000 ft col and on to the summit.
A summer visit via the maintained Crater Creek/Crater Lakes Trail (7.8 miles round trip to the lake) could reasonably be done as a single long day or a lighter two-day trip with a camp at the lake.

contradictions.why: The header Dist stat (from dist_km) would show only the distance to Crater Lake, not the full route, since the route continues off-trail from the lake up the ridge to the ~8,000 ft col and the summit — a real but unquantified additional distance the same fields describe.
contradictions.internal_resolution: dist_km (3.9 mi one-way) numerically matches the '3.9 miles one-way to Crater Lake' trail-only segment quoted in the approach text and itinerary's 7.8 mi round-trip-to-the-lake figure, confirming it excludes the off-trail summit portion.

claims.says: Raven Ridge / Corax Peak summit (elev 8572)
A separate, lower sub-summit called "Corax" (~8,380 ft) sits just west of the main summit saddle.

contradictions.why: This route's summit waypoint labels the true 8,572 ft summit as 'Corax Peak', but the area's other route describes Corax as a distinct, lower (~8,380 ft) false summit west of the main saddle — a climber could be confused about which point is the true high point.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The Standard Route's beta is explicit and detailed about Corax being a separate lower point (and both routes' own watch_out/pro_tips warn about a lower false summit near the saddle); the SE Ridge route's waypoint name conflating Corax with the true summit appears to be the error.

~5.1-5.5 mi one-way...to Libby Lake

contradictions.internal_resolution: The pitch_detail's own one-way trail distance (~5.1-5.5 mi) doubled (~10.2-11 mi) agrees with the itinerary's stated 10-11 mile round trip; dist_km is the outlier.

contradictions.fact: whether a parking pass is required at Libby Lake Trailhead

claims.says: The Forest Service states that no parking fee or pass is required at the Libby Lake Trailhead, though some parties report that a Northwest Forest Pass is expected — confirm current signage locally
Conflicting reports — the Forest Service says none is required at Libby Lake Trailhead, but a Northwest Forest Pass is also reported as needed

contradictions.why: The row itself documents an unresolved conflict about whether a pass is required, which could leave a climber unsure whether to buy one before driving out.

claims.says: Strong multi-day hiking fitness - approach is long and remote (typically via high camp in Leroy or Phelps Creek basin), often paired with summiting Emerald Peak the same trip
Fox Camp (Pyramid Creek Trail junction)

Standard access is the North Fork Entiat River Trail (#1437)...to the Pyramid Creek/Fern Lake trail junction...most parties camp either at Fox Camp near the junction or push on to a larch-meadow camp directly beneath the Emerald-Saska col
Reach camp near the Emerald-Saska basin (~6,800-7,200 ft)

contradictions.why: Leroy Basin and Phelps Creek belong to a different drainage system (the Chiwawa-side approach to Mount Fernow, referenced elsewhere in this catalog's Entiat-area data), not this route's North Fork Entiat/Fox Camp approach — a climber reading only this field could plan a trip to the wrong valley entirely.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Every other field on this route (6 GPS waypoints, approach text, all 3 itinerary days, the road/road driveNote, and the bivy list) consistently and specifically describes the North Fork Entiat Trail to Fox Camp/the Emerald-Saska basin; the 'Leroy or Phelps Creek basin' mention is inconsistent with all of them and appears to be contaminated text copied from a different peak's route data.

contradictions.fact: whether the route is ever climbed in avalanche season

claims.says: N/A - non-glaciated summer scramble route; NWAC does not issue a forecast specific to the Entiat Mountains and this route is not climbed in avalanche season
Essentially a winter snow climb through May in most years, with avalanche and steep-snow hazard on the southwest face; attempted mainly by ski-mountaineers.

Full winter mountaineering/ski-mountaineering conditions and serious avalanche terrain; a documented February 2020 ascent via the Grouse Creek/southwest-face line is described as a probable first winter ascent.
a documented February 2020 winter-ascent party lost a ski over these cliffs after misjudging the descent line in icy conditions

contradictions.why: The row itself documents a real, named winter ascent with avalanche/steep-snow hazard on the southwest face, directly contradicting the avalanche field's unqualified claim that the route is never climbed in avalanche season; a winter/spring party reading only that field could wrongly conclude there's no avalanche exposure to plan for.
contradictions.internal_resolution: climate.bySeason (spring and winter) and descent_text corroborate each other describing a real, documented winter ascent with avalanche hazard; seasonal_hazards.avalanche.zone's 'not climbed in avalanche season' clause is the outlier, evidently intended to be scoped to the July-September monthBreakdown but stated as an unqualified claim about the whole route.
